notes: a. Items 1,3,4,5,6,8 have no alternative future use (or are R&D services/labor/overhead/preproduction prototypes of an asset still under development) and are expensed as R&D when incurred = $1454000. Items 2 and 7 have significant alternative future uses across multiple projects, so they are capitalized ($600000 and $40000) and charged to R&D through depreciation/amortization. Item 9 (quality control during commercial production) and item 10 (corporate G&A not clearly related to R&D) are ordinary operating expenses, not R&D. e. Year 1 disclosed R&D = $1578000.00. Excluded: QC on commercial production $35000; corporate G&A $200000; the capitalized cost of the lab equipment $600000 and of the technical license $40000 (only the $114000.00 depreciation and $10000.00 amortization enter R&D in Year 1). f. Jan 1 Yr 4: cost $600000 less accumulated depreciation $342000.00 = book value $258000.00; proceeds $240000 produce a loss of $18000.00. g. The equipment is not fully expensed in Year 1 because it has significant alternative future uses — it is a productive asset that will serve future R&D projects and production support, so it meets the definition of an asset and is capitalized. Its service potential is nevertheless consumed by R&D activity, so each period's depreciation is the portion of the asset's cost used up in R&D and is classified as R&D expense in that period. Equipment devoted to a single project with no alternative use (item 3) has no future service potential beyond that project and is expensed immediately.
